premises: W–Cu composites suffer from phase separation and interfacial void formation during high-temperature processing and service.
An ultrathin (1–5 nm) Ta film can be deposited conformally on W surfaces via ALD.
A Ta interlayer acts as an effective diffusion barrier between W and Cu at ~1200°C consolidation and up to ~400°C service.
Suppressing interdiffusion and void formation at the W/Cu interface improves thermal conductivity.
The Ta barrier remains stable and effective under irradiation conditions relevant to plasma-facing components.
